solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ends from what you hear in revolutionary act

indicators.note: the ends of the four words that follow are taken, one final letter from each

explanation.surface: Something in what you hear brings an end to a revolutionary act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends from' takes the last letters of 'what you hear in'. Those make T, U, R, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotation or spin is an act of going round, a revolution in the literal sense.

clue.text: Studying this should help you get the next answer

definitions.text: Studying this should help you get the next answer

parts.words: Studying this should help you get the next answer
parts.note: the next answer is 2 Down, a word for faith, and the academic study of faith and divinity would help you get it

explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the next light, 2 Down, whose answer means 'faith'. The subject that studies faith and God is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Divinity is the academic subject studying God and belief, the natural preparation for a clue about faith.

clue.text: Faith is what's central to belief covered by tract

indicators.note: covered by says the central letters sit inside the word for a tract, wrapped by it

parts.note: a tract is an area of land, a region

indicators.note: what's central to picks out the middle letters of the word belief

explanation.surface: Faith is what lies at the heart of belief, as set out in a religious tract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' suggests a religious pamphlet, which suits the surface, but here it means a stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A faith is a system of worship and belief, such as Christianity or Islam.

clue.text: Grilling from a lot of lawyers and copper in person

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers as a whole

indicators.note: in places the symbol for copper inside the word for a person

parts.note: a being is a person or creature
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A cross-examination by a crowd of lawyers and a policeman in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grilling' and 'copper' (slang for a policeman) suggest an interrogation, but the grilling is cookery and copper is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking food over an open flame or hot coals outdoors is the same as grilling it.

clue.text: Get older kind of contract, a factor in Scotland

parts.note: to get older is to age
in bridge, a no-trumps contract is written NT

explanation.surface: Growing older brings a new type of contract for an estate manager in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a factor is the person who manages an estate for its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish factor acts on behalf of a landowner, so is a representative managing property for someone else.

clue.text: A crime lab rebuilt, using two houses

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters of the three words are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A forensic laboratory has been reconstructed and now occupies two buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' look like buildings for the lab, but they are chambers of a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislature with two chambers, like a Commons and a Lords, is described with this term.

clue.text: With maximum speed, somehow send on report as journalist

parts.note: c is the speed of light, the greatest possible speed

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the following three words are arranged in some new way

explanation.surface: A journalist told to file a report as quickly as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With maximum speed' reads as hurry, but gives C, the physics symbol for the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper reporter covering a particular subject or place, such as a war or foreign capital, carries this title.

clue.text: Here is how the French put it, with minimal friendliness

parts.note: the French word for here is ici

parts.words: is how the French put it
parts.note: the French for is is est, and the phrase also covers the preceding word

explanation.surface: A French speaker states something coolly and without warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How the French put it' applies to both words: 'here is' in French is ICI EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldest in manner means having the least warmth or friendliness, a superlative of frosty.

clue.text: A lot of stars as well as unknowns supporting festivity

indicators.note: in a down light, supporting means placed underneath, so the unknowns come after

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: Plenty of celebrities, along with some nobodies, propping up a festive event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' and 'unknowns' suggest celebrities and nobodies at a gala; the stars are literal and the unknowns are algebra's X and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge system of stars bound together by gravity, such as the Milky Way, is this.

clue.text: East European holding parts of film to screen, more or less

indicators.note: holding means the two letters wrap around the film pieces

parts.note: E for East and E for European
clips are short extracts from a film

explanation.surface: An Eastern European showing bits of a movie on screen, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To screen' suggests showing a film, but here it means to block from view; 'more or less' allows for a partial covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure or overshadow something, as the moon hides the sun, is roughly to shield it from view.

clue.text: Equipment soldier put on rickety airplane outside hospital

indicators.note: in a down light, put on means placed on top, so the soldier comes first

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters go around the hospital letter
rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A soldier loads his kit onto a shaky aircraft parked outside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rickety' turns AIRPLANE into PERNALIA, which goes 'outside' H to give PHERNALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneous gear and accessories needed for an activity are collectively known by this word.

clue.text: Friendly daughter I dressed in pink, sort of

indicators.note: dressed in says the letters are clothed by the colour word

parts.note: coral is a shade of pinkish red

explanation.surface: A friendly father says he dressed his daughter in a pinkish outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm and genial in manner, as a cordial welcome is, means much the same as amiable.

clue.text: Part of table no longer needed — in short, it's a piece of wood

definitions.text: Part of table no longer needed — in short, it's a piece of wood

parts.words: Part of table no longer needed — in short, it's a piece of wood
parts.note: mathematical tables of these values were made obsolete by calculators, and the usual abbreviation of the word is log, a piece of timber

explanation.walkthrough: The 'table' is a printed book of mathematical values, not furniture. Its entries are abbreviated LOG, which is also a piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Log tables listed the exponents used for multiplication by addition, now done by calculators.

clue.text: County taking part in meaningless exercise

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A county joining in a pointless drill.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'meaninglESS EXercise'. Essex is an English county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is one of the home counties of England, bordering London to the north-east.

clue.text: Kind of treatment one can't have

definitions.text: Kind of treatment one can't have

parts.words: Kind of treatment one can't have
parts.note: this psychological treatment is given to several people together, so a single person cannot have it alone

explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like 'a person in general', but is taken literally: a lone individual can't make up a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychotherapy carried out with several patients together in one session is a recognised kind of treatment.

clue.text: Let out clutch and reverse vehicle

parts.note: to hatch a clutch of eggs is to let the chicks out
to reverse is to back

explanation.surface: Driving instructions: release the clutch and back the car up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' looks like the car pedal, but it is a batch of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a rear door hinged at the top that opens upwards is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: It's introduced before end of term merriment

indicators.note: introduced before end of says the letters go in just before the final letter of the term

parts.note: Hilary is the name of the spring term at Oxford and some other universities
read as it is, with it being the word introduced

explanation.surface: Fun is brought in just before the end of the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is the spring term at Oxford University and in the English law courts; IT goes in before its final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud laughter and great amusement are both covered by this word for merriment.

clue.text: Generally incomplete, with dope and everything switched, it produces nasty reaction

indicators.note: switched says the two pieces trade places within the shortened word
with joins the second piece to the swap described by switched
incomplete means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everything
gen is slang for information, as is dope

explanation.surface: As a rule, a partial mix of drugs and everything else triggers a bad reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' cuts GENERALLY to GENERALL; 'switched' swaps its GEN (dope) and ALL (everything), leaving ER in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance such as pollen that triggers an immune response like hay fever is an irritant of this kind.

clue.text: Pressure in satellite wrong, leading to a lot of illness

definitions.text: leading to a lot of illness

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are put together in an incorrect, scrambled order

explanation.surface: A pressure fault in a satellite went wrong and made many people sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but its letters join P and SATELLITE in the pool rearranged by 'wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that spreads plague or deadly disease is described as harmful in this way.

clue.text: Accordingly including clue for traditional faith

indicators.note: including says the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: so means accordingly, therefore
a hint is a clue

explanation.surface: A traditional religion, accordingly, includes a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient native religion of Japan, centred on nature spirits, is a traditional faith.

clue.text: Nut finally put on bolt — that's right?

indicators.note: in a down light, put on means placed on top, so this letter comes first
finally picks out the last letter of the word nut

parts.note: a rivet is a metal bolt or pin for fastening

explanation.surface: A mechanic asks if a nut is finally put on the bolt correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'right as a trivet' means perfectly all right, so the answer is something that is proverbially right.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as right as a trivet', meaning thoroughly sound, makes a trivet the standard of being right.

clue.text: Fowl, including rook, duck, and wading bird

indicators.note: including says the bird word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a hen is a domestic fowl
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A list of birds: a fowl, a rook, a duck, and a wader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' and 'duck' seem to be more birds, but give R (chess) and O (cricket's zero).
explanation.definitionFit: A tall grey long-legged bird that stands in shallow water to catch fish is a classic wader.

clue.text: How to combine handles, for example, with short line

definitions.text: How to combine handles, for example, with short line

parts.words: How to combine handles, for example, with short line
parts.note: handles are names, and double-barrelled names are joined with a short dash between them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handles' look like door handles, but are names; two names are joined with a short line between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining two words with a short dash, as in a double-barrelled surname, is the verb meant.

clue.text: What gets waiter angry, upset, is something upwardly mobile type hammers home

definitions.text: something upwardly mobile type hammers home

indicators.note: in a down light, upset means turned upside down, so the phrase is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a waiter is annoyed at getting no tip

explanation.surface: A waiter left no gratuity is upset, much as a climber hammering something in.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'upwardly mobile type' is not a social climber but a rock climber, who drives this metal spike into the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal peg hammered into a crack in rock to hold a rope is a climber's anchor.

clue.text: Composer and dramatist abridged a piece of fiction

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer, actor and playwright

explanation.surface: A composer and playwright cut down a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a popular Welsh composer and dramatist of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A short novel or long short story is a work of prose fiction of this kind.

clue.text: Supporting church, in a way — after short time, I object

indicators.note: after says the remaining words follow the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Someone objects, after a moment, to paying money to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest, but it is a noun: a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a tenth of one's income to the church is a traditional way of financially supporting it.

clue.text: Excelling in status, was faster than man on board

parts.note: to have outrun someone is to have been faster
the king is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: A runner was quicker than a chess player and so rose above the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a crew member, but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Being higher in rank than others means surpassing them in standing or status.

clue.text: Holy men, being extremely selective, perform religious works

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of each of the two words are selected

explanation.surface: Holy men, being very choosy, carry out religious duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely selective' takes the first and last letters of 'Holy' and 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to sing songs of praise, the religious works in question.
